tagline: Rolling hills, a bayou port and a home for zydeco
intro: Near Ville Platte, Chicot State Park has rolling hills surrounding a man-made lake. Ville Platte itself occupies relatively flat ground, contrasting with the hillier country to its north. Melville lies on mostly flat land inside a ring levee built to protect it from the Atchafalaya River and the West Atchafalaya Floodway. Music gives these towns another point of interest: Ville Platte has a swamp pop museum in a former railway station, and Opelousas is a center of zydeco.

Water crossings changed travel here: the Krotz Springs Bridge opened across the Atchafalaya in 1928, carrying trains and automobiles. Other bridges replaced it at the same location in 1934, 1973 and 1988.

Begin at Bayou Chicot, due north of Ville Platte. In Ville Platte, US 167 runs through town as Main and Lasalle streets. Washington brings the history of an inland port; Krotz Springs brings the Atchafalaya River. Port Barre sits where Bayou Courtableau and Bayou Teche meet, east of Opelousas. Continue west to Eunice, then Basile, both on US 190.

moments.title: Chicot State Park
moments.text: Lake Chicot is a made landscape: a 2,000-acre artificial lake surrounded by rolling hills in a 6,400-acre park near Ville Platte. The park entered the Louisiana state system in 1939, and the Civilian Conservation Corps developed much of the area under National Park Service direction. A hiking and backpacking trail circles the lake, with primitive campsites along it. The lake supports largemouth bass, crappie, bluegill and red-ear sunfish. The Louisiana State Arboretum State Preservation Area is at the South Landing.
moments.notice: Rolling hills surround the man-made lake.

moments.title: Washington
moments.text: Founded as a French trading post in 1764, Washington later had a problem for steamboats: they could reach the village but could not turn around. The boats came up Bayou Teche, passed Barre’s Landing and continued along Bayou Courtableau. In 1848, Captain George W. Haygood completed a turnaround, and Washington became an inland port. The Washington Historic District entered the National Register of Historic Places in 1978. At the time of listing, the district included 200 contributing buildings and three contributing sites.

moments.title: Opelousas
moments.text: Zydeco has a home in Opelousas, which has hosted the Original Southwest Louisiana Zydeco Festival since 1982. The festival moved from Zydeco Park in Plaisance to the Yambilee Festival grounds in Opelousas. Its musicians perform with the aim of keeping the genre alive. Music also reaches listeners through KOCZ-LP, a community radio station owned and operated by the Southern Development Foundation. Volunteers from Opelousas and across the country built the station at the third Prometheus Radio Project barnraising. Its programming includes music, news and public affairs for listeners at 92.9.
